body: I understand it's due to backward compatibility, but personally, I don't like it here. It looks like it won't be possible to create a MeshInstance3D as a child of a skeleton without being "automagically" forced to use it (other than by selecting a different skeleton).
I mean I added to not anger the compatibility overlords but I am fine with removing it.

@patwork Can you explain your use case? If a mesh without any bones "uses" a Skeleton3D, it won't do anything.

I'd argue this change is a good idea even without compatibility concerns. Using the parent as a skeleton by default makes sense to me, which means using the parent when the NodePath is empty.

I'm very confused. The PR description says

> In order to keep compatibility with the current weirdness I made it look at the parent node when the skeleton_path is empty. If the parent node is a skeleton it is used as a fallback to simulate the old (..) parent nodepath behavior.

If this is removed, then how will this not break compatibility. We can't both keep this default and then also remove it.

Also, what is the advantage of having a case where skeleton is null?

I do kind of wish there was an easier way to tell if a mesh instance is skinned (and then, the skeleton and skin properties can be removed from non-skinned meshes)

I was in the middle of updating the description lyuma.

If we decide to remove this comp code with auto skeleton parent it breaks comp for those projects with a skeleton parent that relied on this behavior.

Those projects that already have a different nodepath are unaffected because that path would be stored in the node variable within the scene file.

I dont want to touch the skin part here. I think it should be solved as well because creating a new skin ref on every update attempt with no skeleton in use is kinda a waste, but that is its own minor issue to solve.

OK, my only concern is that the engine would force-connect the parent skeleton to the mesh without asking the user. In the editor, the skeleton node would be 'null', but this would change behind the scenes after running the project. This could be confusing for the user.

I guess there are two options:

1. leave force-connect (backward compatible) but state in documentation that engine will do it automatically for the user
2. remove backward compatibility, but warn users about it in migration guide (and also check other places in the engine if they are setting skeleton path correctly, like scene importer)
@patwork Why is it bad to force-connect a MeshInstance3D to its parent node when there is no other skeleton?

because "force" ;) And because it's done in the runtime and not clearly visible in the editor. If the runtime connects mesh instances when their skeleton paths are null, it will not be possible to disable skeleton connection when the user wants it (other than moving specified mesh somewhere else in the tree).

Having auto-to-parent attachment behavior can work with node classes that are very narrow in scope, e.g. NavigationAgent attaching to a parent or collision shapes attaching to the body node.

MeshInstance3D is more or less the base node for anything 3d visual that people use in projects, addons, and what not at very inflated amount. So many addons alone build their custom nodes by inheriting MeshInstance3D. If they would all auto snap to skeletons that would be a disaster. For a node class as broadly used like MeshInstance3D for many things it is just bad design and a tripwire to have such auto behavior.

Just my two cents, I think that assigning Skeleton3D to MeshInstance is the role of the importer scene, not role of the MeshInstance itself.

I guess that MeshInstance automatically assigns Skeleton3D is perhaps due to the old behavior of the importer, or maybe it was a hack to treat fbx and gltf equally, but I don't know much about it. In the first place, if parent-child relationships are to be enforce, I don't think the path item is necessary.

Considering that, was the assumption of specifying the path without parent-child relationships in the MeshInstance present in the old importer?

As with removing the path from BoneAttachment3D in ModifierBoneTarget3D, one way might be to prepare two classes, one that forces parent-child attachment without path (as `SkeletonMesh3D`) and one that does not but is having path (as `MeshInstance3D`), and allow users to choose which one to use during migration.

Alternatively, it may be possible to just add a property called `Use External Skeleton`, similar to BoneAttachment.
